concern.concern: The uniform needle bound lacks a uniform separation hypothesis. Step 1.2 says, “compactness and embeddedness give a uniform positive lower bound for |z-z′|,” but embeddedness for each ε and compact control of the critical-point charts do not prevent another regular strand from approaching the needle as ε→0. Locally take the fixed Morse cap z=s, t=−s², |s|≤ε/2, and another upward strand z=iε. The cap has horizontal diameter ε and its critical chart is unchanged. Its two signed degree-one mixed-chord integrals sum, up to orientation sign, to (2πi)⁻¹ log((1/2−i)/(−1/2−i)), a nonzero constant; the chord joins different skeleton components and survives tangle 1T. These local pieces can be extended by regular arcs inside a fixed slab. Thus the written chart assumptions do not justify Cmε uniformly. The cited CDM §8.6.2 argument also uses opposite-branch cancellation rather than the claimed individual absolute long-chord estimate. The convergence assertion for a fixed tangle is a separate issue.

original_concerns.reason: Embeddedness of each positive-epsilon member and compact control of only critical charts do not give a lower bound uniform in epsilon for a long-chord denominator. The local cap z=s,t=-s^2, |s|<=epsilon/2 and upward strand z=i epsilon have fixed Morse germ and remain embedded for every epsilon>0. The opposite down-sign mixed terms integrate to the oriented cap integral (2pi i)^(-1) integral_{-epsilon/2}^{epsilon/2} ds/(s-i epsilon), which after s=epsilon u is a fixed nonzero constant. The chord connects different skeleton components and survives tangle 1T. A smooth regular continuation inside the slab can meet fixed exterior endpoints; no uniform exterior separation is in the contract. Hence the stated uniform O(epsilon) conclusion and step 1.2 are unjustified as written. This does not refute absolute convergence for each fixed tangle.

case.uncertainty: The cap counterexample settles the missing-uniformity concern. The proposed added chart controls are sufficient for the written absolute-estimate proof; no assertion is made that they are necessary or optimally weak. In particular, width alone need not bound the entire Morse-parameter range for a long thin tail; the proposed local-cap branch states that condition explicitly. This report does not claim a full new reconstruction of the cited general cancellation theorem.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: For every fixed $m$, the sum of degree-$m$ pairing integrals that have at least one endpoint on $N_\varepsilon$ has norm at most $C_m\varepsilon$, where $C_m$ is independent of $\varepsilon$. Thus these contributions tend to zero as the needle narrows.
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: For the following uniform local-cap estimate, assume additionally a fixed finite system of disjoint critical bands and intervening regular bands, with uniformly bounded branch derivatives in their height or Morse coordinates. Assume the critical charts vary in a compact smooth family and their linear terms are uniformly bounded away from zero, and that every equal-height pair other than the two branches meeting at the same critical point has horizontal separation at least a fixed $d>0$, independent of $\varepsilon$. Require $N_\varepsilon$ to lie in one of these Morse charts with parameter range $0\le s\le A\varepsilon$, for a fixed $A$. Then, for every fixed $m$, the sum of degree-$m$ pairing integrals with at least one endpoint on $N_\varepsilon$ has norm at most $C_m\varepsilon$, with $C_m$ independent of $\varepsilon$. Thus these contributions tend to zero under these uniformity hypotheses. No such uniform estimate is asserted for an unrelated strand approaching the needle as $\varepsilon\to0$; convergence for each fixed knot or tangle is unaffected.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: 1.2 For a long chord with one endpoint on the needle and one outside it, compactness and embeddedness give a uniform positive lower bound for $|z-z'|$ on each compact branch chart. In the Morse parameter $s$, both endpoint evaluations are smooth, so the one-form $d\log(z-z')$ has norm at most $C\,ds$. The range of $s$ along a width-$\varepsilon$ needle is at most $C\varepsilon$, since $|z_+(s)-z_-(s)|\asymp s$. Thus integrating such a chord endpoint over any subinterval of the needle costs at most $C\varepsilon$. This is a direct absolute estimate for each pairing term and does not identify diagrams obtained from opposite branch choices. The constants are uniform in the stated compact smooth family. [given, F1, F2, construct, algebra]
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: 1.2 For a fixed knot or tangle, a long chord in a sufficiently small critical chart has nonzero limiting separation at the critical point, so its denominator is bounded below by some positive constant. In the uniform local-cap family, the additional separation hypothesis supplies the same lower bound $d$ independently of $\varepsilon$. The branch derivative bounds in the Morse parameter give $|d(z-z')|\le C\,ds$, hence $|d\log(z-z')|\le (C/d)\,ds$ uniformly. The stipulated range $0\le s\le A\varepsilon$ then bounds the integral of this factor by $CA\varepsilon/d$; on a subinterval $(0,\delta)$ it is at most $C\delta/d$. These are individual absolute estimates under the stated uniformity hypotheses. They do not replace the opposite-branch cancellation used for more general special critical movements in the cited sources. [given, F1, F2, construct, algebra]
